title: Navratri Watchlist: Bollywood Films With Garba Scenes Worth Revisiting
excerpt: From "Dholi Taro Dhol Baaje" to "Dholida," eight films whose garba and dandiya sequences make the perfect one-a-night viewing across the festival.
body:
• Sharad Navratri begins October 11, 2026. For the nine nights, here are eight Bollywood films whose garba and dandiya sequences capture the festival better than any playlist, from the 1999 gold standard to last year's romances.
  • The Bhansali trio anchors any watchlist: Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam ("Dholi Taro Dhol Baaje"), Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela ("Nagada Sang Dhol"), and Gangubai Kathiawadi ("Dholida").
  • The festival drives the plot in Loveyatri, Kai Po Che!, and Satyaprem Ki Katha, where romances begin in the whirl of dandiya sticks and Navratri nights carry the story's emotional turns.
  • Reader utility: most of the list is streaming now. Per OTTplay, Ram-Leela, Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam, Satyaprem Ki Katha, and Kai Po Che! are on Prime Video (Kai Po Che! is also on Netflix), Raees is on Netflix, and Loveyatri is free on YouTube. That is one film per night with nights to spare.

The gold standard

No Navratri watchlist can start anywhere but 1999. In Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam, Sanjay Leela Bhansali staged "Dholi Taro Dhol Baaje" as a full-throated celebration of Gujarati festive culture: Salman Khan and Aishwarya Rai dancing garba in elaborate traditional dress, choreographed by Vaibhavi Merchant, who won the National Film Award for Best Choreography for it. Composed by Ismail Darbar and sung by Kavita Krishnamurthy, Vinod Rathod, and Karsan Sargathia, the sequence made Bollywood's portrayal of Navratri synonymous with grandeur. Twenty-seven years later it remains the reference point every later garba number is measured against.

Bhansali's festival spectacles

Bhansali returned to the form twice more, each time bigger. In Goliyon Ki Raasleela Ram-Leela (2013), Deepika Padukone's "Nagada Sang Dhol" is one of the most intense depictions of Navratri on screen: a traditional Gujarati outfit, a surging crowd, and a performance that carries the film's emotional weight, not just its festive color. The song, sung by Shreya Ghoshal and Osman Mir, is now a garba-night staple in its own right. In Gangubai Kathiawadi (2022), Alia Bhatt's "Dholida," choreographed by Kruti Mahesh and sung by Janhvi Shrimankar and Shail Hada, threads devotion through a story of grit and feminine power. Devdas (2002) belongs in this company too: "Dola Re Dola," though not a Navratri number, was filmed against a grand Durga Puja mandap, and its scale and energy made it an honorary festival classic.

Films where Navratri drives the plot

The most interesting Navratri films are the ones where the festival is not decoration but engine. Loveyatri (2018) is built around the nine nights themselves, a romance that unfolds across garba evenings, and its song "Chogada" became the garba anthem of its release year. Kai Po Che! (2013) uses Navratri as an authentic Gujarati backdrop for its story of friendship; Rajkummar Rao and Amrita Puri dancing to Amit Trivedi's soulful "Shubhaarambh" is one of the film's most beloved passages. Satyaprem Ki Katha (2023) opens in the thick of the festival, with Kartik Aaryan's Sattu first seeing Kiara Advani's Katha amid the whirl of sticks and steps, and the "Sun Sajni" number captures the communal joy of dandiya nights. Raees (2017) gives the festival a tenser register: Shah Rukh Khan's powerful garba performance to "Udi Udi Jaye" presents Navratri with both solemnity and high energy.

The new entry

Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani (2023) is the most recent addition to the canon. Karan Johar's "Dhindora Baje Re," staged during Durga Puja with couture-level costumes and cross-generational warmth, reminded audiences that Bollywood still treats the autumn festival season as prime cinematic real estate. It is the lightest film on this list and the easiest post-dance wind-down.

The diaspora angle

In diaspora households, these films do quiet cultural work. Children who have never stood in a garba circle in Gujarat learn the steps, the outfits, and the social grammar of the festival from these sequences before they ever try the real thing. Family movie nights during the nine days have become a tradition of their own in Indian homes abroad: one film a night, ending with Dussehra on October 20.

What's next

Nine nights, eight films, and one spare evening for the season's new trailer drops. Start with the 1999 classic tonight and move forward in time; by the time Alia Bhatt's "Dholida" closes the run, the festival will have made its point. Bollywood has been filming Navratri for nearly three decades. This is the week to watch it all back.
